characterization_methods: 51V solid state nuclear magnetic resonance (51V NMR)
evidence: The catalysts were characterized by chemical analysis, BET surface area measurements, X-ray diffraction (XRD), electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and 51V solid state nuclear magnetic resonance (51V NMR). The degree and temperature of reduction of the active species in correlation with their dispersion were determined by temperature programmed reduction (TPR) in argon-diluted dihydrogen gas flow. The number, strength and strength distribution of the surface acidic sites were examined by ammonia adsorption microcalorimetry and the nature of the acidic sites by infrared (IR) spectroscopy after pyridine adsorption. The specific surface area of the catalysts was calculated by the BET method of nitrogen adsorption at 77 K after heat pretreatment under vacuum for 4 h at 673 K. XRD measurements were carried out in a Bruker D5005 diffractometer between 3 and 80 (2θ) at 50 kV and 35 mA, using Cu K /H9251radiation (λ = 0.015418 nm). XPS data were collected in a VG Escalab 200R instrument (11 kV , 20 mA) applying non monochromatic Mg K /H9251radiation source (1253.6 eV). The 51V chemical shifts were calibrated against liquid VOCl 3, using a 0.16 M NaVO 3 aqueous solution (chemical shift at − 574.3 ppm) as a secondary reference. The EPR spectra were recorded with a Varian E9 101 spectrometer equipped with a dual cavity using the 9.4 GHz (X band of Klystron E 101 Microwave Bridge) microwave frequency. The 51V NMR spectra were recorded at ambient conditions with a Bruker DSX400 (9.4 T) NMR spectrometer operating at 105.2 MHz under static conditions. The pyridine adsorption IR spectra were recorded with a Bruker Vector 22 FTIR spectrophotometer (DTGS detector). The differential heats of adsorption were measured as a function of coverage by repeatedly sending small doses of ammonia gas onto the catalyst until an equilibrium pressure of about 66 Pa was reached.
